title: Learn Application Security
tagline: Secure software by design — find flaws early, fix them responsibly
description: A three-level curriculum for Application Security Engineers. Learn how modern apps fail, how to review and test them with authorization, and how to embed defenses into design, CI/CD, and incident response — always within legal and ethical boundaries.
prerequisites: Comfort with at least one programming language (e.g. Python, JavaScript, Java, or Go)
Basic web concepts: HTTP, cookies, sessions, and APIs
Willingness to work only on systems you own or have written permission to test

levels.title: Secure Development Foundations
levels.goal: Explain common web risks and apply basic secure-coding and review habits

topics.title: Authorized testing only
items: Written permission, scopes, and rules of engagement
What is out of scope and how to stop immediately
Responsible disclosure and coordinated vulnerability reporting

topics.title: AppSec roles & outcomes
items: How AppSec partners with engineering and product
Shift-left vs. runtime defenses
Risk language: likelihood, impact, and business context

topics.title: HTTP & trust boundaries
items: Requests, responses, headers, and cookies
Client vs. server trust — never trust input
Sessions, tokens, and authentication basics

topics.title: OWASP Top 10 overview
items: Injection, XSS, and broken access control at a conceptual level
Misconfiguration and vulnerable components
Mapping findings to remediation owners

topics.title: Input handling
items: Validation, encoding, and parameterized queries
File uploads and path traversal defenses
Secrets: never commit keys; use env/secret stores

topics.title: First security reviews
items: Reading a PR with a security checklist
Spotting hardcoded credentials and debug endpoints
Documenting issues without blame

projects: Write a one-page rules-of-engagement template for an internal lab app
Map the attack surface of a simple web app (routes, auth, data stores)
Fix three intentional insecure patterns in a training codebase (with tests)
Produce a beginner AppSec checklist for pull-request review

levels.title: Assessment & Pipeline Security
levels.goal: Run authorized assessments and wire security checks into the delivery pipeline

topics.title: Diagrams & STRIDE
items: Data-flow diagrams for a feature or service
STRIDE categories applied to real components
Prioritizing threats that matter to the business

topics.title: Abuse cases
items: Turning user stories into abuse cases
AuthZ matrix: who can do what on which resource
Feeding model outputs into backlog items

topics.title: Static & dependency analysis
items: Running Semgrep or similar SAST on a repo
SCA for known vulnerable libraries and licenses
Triage: false positives vs. real risk

topics.title: Dynamic testing (authorized)
items: Baseline scans with ZAP or Burp against a lab target
Manual verification of automated findings
Safe handling of credentials and scan data

topics.title: API security
items: Broken object-level authorization (BOLA/IDOR) patterns
Rate limiting, pagination, and mass assignment
OpenAPI reviews for over-exposed fields

topics.title: AuthN / AuthZ deep dive
items: OAuth/OIDC pitfalls (redirects, scopes, token storage)
Session fixation, CSRF, and cookie flags
Multi-tenant isolation checks

topics.title: Pipeline controls
items: Failing builds on high-severity SAST/SCA findings
Secret scanning in CI
Signed commits and protected branches as security controls

projects: Threat model a feature end-to-end and file prioritized backlog tickets
Add SAST + SCA to CI with a documented triage process
Authorized API assessment report for a lab service (findings + remediations)
Design an authZ test matrix and automate a few critical cases

levels.title: Program Design & Resilience
levels.goal: Lead AppSec programs that prevent, detect, and respond at scale

topics.title: Program building blocks
items: Security champions, training, and office hours
Risk acceptance and exception workflows
Metrics that drive behavior (not vanity scan counts)

topics.title: Architecture reviews
items: Reviewing new services before build
Trust zones, zero-trust assumptions, and shared libraries
Supply-chain: SBOM, provenance, and signed artifacts

topics.title: Deep assessments
items: Combining automated coverage with focused manual testing
Business-logic flaws that scanners miss
Coordinating with pen-test partners under clear scope

topics.title: Vulnerability management
items: Severity, SLA, and retest cycles
Responsible disclosure intake and researcher communication
Public CVE process awareness (when you are a vendor)

topics.title: From finding to fix in production
items: WAF/RASP as compensating controls — not substitutes for fixes
Working with SOC on app-layer signals
Post-incident: root cause, secure redesign, and lessons learned

topics.title: Compliance as engineering
items: Mapping controls to OWASP ASVS / NIST CSF language
Evidence collection without theater
Privacy and security overlap (data minimization, logging hygiene)

projects: Draft an AppSec program charter with metrics, SLAs, and exception policy
Run a tabletop for a critical web vuln disclosure and document the playbook
Design a secure reference architecture for a multi-tenant SaaS API
Build an ASVS-inspired control checklist mapped to your stack
